title: Turn an observed workflow into a testable offer
task: Draft the next commercial experiment offer for the warehouse manager and recommend the commitment it can support.

facts.S-BRIEF: Three recent weekly stock reconciliations each consumed four manager hours. The manager supplies approved deidentified CSVs; the COO controls purchasing. The founder permits proposing a one-week manual service at a test price between USD 400 and 600. Nothing has been quoted or accepted.
facts.S-CAPACITY: The operator has six hours next week. The proposed artifact is an exception report linking unmatched rows to supplied records. Inventory corrections and system integrations are outside this test. Outreach is not commissioned.

anchors: Drafts a bounded one-week exception-report offer for the manager with the COO identified as payer.
Labels a price within the authorized range as proposed and defines observable report acceptance and timing.
Includes exclusions and a proposed failure/rework route; recommends preparation rather than claiming accepted commercial terms.
alternatives: Any authorized test price and reasonable bounded acceptance or rework terms are valid if explicitly proposed.

title: Useful does not accept the quoted purchase
task: Review the forecast entry and draft the smallest useful follow-up before committing delivery hours.

facts.S-EMAIL: The seller emailed a USD 900 quote for a five-day analysis. The prospect replied, 'This looks useful; send me an example report.' No order, price agreement, payment, or delivery date was confirmed.
facts.S-PLAN: The forecast marks the opportunity as a confirmed USD 900 order and reserves nine delivery hours. The founder authorizes one hour to prepare an example from synthetic data; starting customer delivery requires accepted scope and terms.

anchors: Corrects confirmed order status because requesting an example does not accept the price or delivery commitment.
Drafts a useful clarification of scope, price, acceptance and timing without portraying the reply as an agreement.
Allows the authorized synthetic example while holding the nine-hour delivery commitment.
alternatives: A concise example-first follow-up with an explicit purchase decision afterward is valid within the one-hour cap.

title: Discount versus commitment exposure
task: Compare both purchase options over twelve months and recommend which offer to advance under the customer's stated limits.

facts.S-QUOTE: Identical service costs USD 300 monthly, cancellable before each renewal, or USD 3000 paid upfront for twelve months. Both charge USD 200 setup. The annual payment becomes nonrefundable after fourteen days.
facts.S-BUYER: The buyer has USD 3300 available and needs the service for three confirmed months. The buyer permits at most USD 1000 of noncancellable exposure under the contract chosen now, measured after any initial cooling-off window. Monthly renewals remain optional. No purchase has been authorized.

anchors: Computes twelve-month comparable totals and savings with setup included consistently.
Recommends the monthly option under the irrevocable-commitment cap while recognizing the annual price advantage.
Distinguishes twelve-month comparison assumptions from the three-month confirmed need and preserves purchase authority.
alternatives: Negotiating an annual cancellation provision is valid as a proposal; the existing annual terms cannot be treated as compliant.

title: A volume request exceeds the quoted package
task: Recommend a response to the customer's requested scope and prepare a usable next quote direction.

facts.S-RATECARD: The standard package is USD 600 for reviewing up to fifty support tickets. A separate high-volume plan charges USD 1 per ticket with a minimum commitment of five hundred tickets. Custom intermediate pricing is reserved to the founder.
facts.S-REQUEST: A customer wants sixty-one tickets reviewed and says to put all of them in the standard package. The operator may quote published packages but cannot waive limits or invent custom prices. No order is accepted.

anchors: Identifies that sixty-one tickets exceed the standard scope and do not qualify for the high-volume rate.
Proposes a fifty-ticket bounded scope or a concrete founder decision on intermediate pricing.
Requires customer acceptance of the resulting scope and price without inventing a rate or promising unauthorized work.
alternatives: Offering the published high-volume minimum is permissible if its actual commitment is clear and its poor fit is acknowledged.

title: Purchase order changes material terms
task: Assess whether delivery can start from the received purchase order and draft the needed resolution.

facts.S-QUOTE: The seller's approved quote is USD 600 once for a diagnostic report, delivered within seven days, with one correction round during the following week.
facts.S-ORDER: The buyer's purchase order lists USD 600 for weekly diagnostics plus unlimited ongoing support. Its covering email says, 'Please begin under the attached order.' No payment has arrived. The operator may prepare a clarification but only the founder can change price, scope, or recurring obligations.

anchors: Finds the recurring delivery and unlimited-support terms materially inconsistent with the approved one-time quote.
Holds commencement under the mismatched terms and drafts a specific corrected order or founder decision request.
Does not infer that the purchase order or covering email settles the seller's unapproved obligations or proves payment.
alternatives: A separately priced recurring proposal is valid for founder review, provided it is not represented as accepted.

title: Replace an unsupported outcome guarantee
task: Revise the proposed offer into something the operator can responsibly test this week.

facts.S-DRAFT: The draft promises 'reduce your logistics costs by twenty percent in seven days or we pay your losses.' No cost baseline, causal test, loss limit, or customer implementation authority exists.
facts.S-MANDATE: The founder permits a USD 1000 diagnostic using customer-approved shipment records. The operator can identify duplicate charges, document checks, and deliver a prioritized review. The founder has not authorized indemnities, refunds beyond the service fee, or operational changes at the customer.

anchors: Removes the unsupported savings and loss-payment guarantee while preserving a useful bounded diagnostic offer.
Defines acceptance around checkable analysis and documented findings rather than guaranteed customer savings.
Keeps proposed failure terms within authority and identifies baseline or implementation evidence needed for later savings claims.
alternatives: A narrower fee-refund proposal may be prepared for approval if clearly conditional and tied to measurable delivery acceptance.

title: Quote a fourth slot against actual delivery capacity
task: Calculate the proposed cohort's capacity position and recommend terms for the fourth prospect.

facts.S-OFFER: Each USD 900 two-week engagement requires two onboarding hours, five analysis hours and one support hour. Three customers have accepted identical dates; a fourth asks whether a slot is available.
facts.S-ROSTER: The operator has thirty-eight available hours in that same fortnight, including ten already committed to unrelated work. No substitute operator is available. Prices and deliverables are fixed; the founder permits proposing a later start. No fourth engagement has been accepted.

anchors: Includes onboarding, analysis, support and unrelated commitments in the same-period capacity calculation.
Does not promise the fourth simultaneous slot when the complete proposed cohort exceeds available hours.
Recommends a later start or an explicitly reviewed scope/capacity change with customer acceptance.
alternatives: Declining the fourth engagement is valid if no later date suits; unauthorized unpaid overtime is not evidenced capacity.

title: An internal service offer uses an authorized resource envelope
task: Prepare a bounded first-cycle offer for the internal support department's sponsor.

facts.S-MANDATE: The sponsor authorizes twelve staff hours each week to produce a Monday backlog review for the support lead. The lead needs a reproducible count by issue type and three proposed priorities. The sponsor and lead will accept the review together.
facts.S-SCOPE: Source access covers internal ticket aggregates. Staff may analyze and recommend but cannot reassign work or change support policy. There is no external customer, sale, internal fee, or revenue target. The first draft is due next Monday.

anchors: Defines the backlog review, recipients, deadline, exclusions and checkable joint acceptance within twelve staff hours.
Uses the resource envelope as the internal offer constraint without inventing a commercial price or paid demand.
Proposes a proportionate rework/escalation route and next-cycle resource check rather than unauthorized policy execution.
alternatives: A smaller first-week report is valid if its acceptance scope and sponsor approval dependency are explicit.

title: A price test also changed delivery and audience
task: Interpret the existing responses and draft the next experiment that could inform the price decision.

facts.S-TEST: Six warm referrals received a USD 500 offer including onboarding; three requested a call. Six cold accounts received a USD 200 self-service offer; one requested a call. The messages were sent in different weeks. No purchase occurred.
facts.S-DECISION: The founder wants to declare that the higher price increases demand. The operator may draft one experiment with up to twelve qualified accounts, a two-hour preparation cap, and a two-week observation window. Sending requires the existing campaign owner's authorization.

anchors: Explains that audience, onboarding and timing differ, so the observed calls do not isolate a price effect.
Drafts a bounded comparison keeping material nonprice factors comparable and measuring a meaningful purchasing step.
Predeclares a decision rule, owner and horizon while respecting the cap and avoiding a universal sample threshold.
alternatives: Testing one explicit offer before comparing prices is valid if its narrower decision value is explained.

title: Complete terms support preparation of the agreed test
task: Decide the next commitment and specify the immediate preparation needed for the accepted engagement.

facts.S-AGREEMENT: The budget owner accepted a USD 1500 one-time report due in two weeks, payable after acceptance. Acceptance checks reconcile all supplied rows and document exceptions. The agreement includes one correction round, a named support contact and cancellation before data transfer without charge.
facts.S-READINESS: Approved data handling, ten available operator hours, a six-hour delivery estimate, an accountable owner and a USD 100 cost cap are recorded. The commissioned action is preparing the delivery checklist. Nothing has yet been delivered, invoiced or paid.

anchors: Allows preparation of the delivery checklist using the accepted terms and existing authority.
Carries the acceptance checks, support/cancellation route, owner and exposure cap into useful next actions.
Describes accepted terms and experiment readiness without claiming payment, completed delivery or a demonstrated MVC.
alternatives: A concise checklist linked to the existing agreement is sufficient; duplicating a full company pack is unnecessary.

title: Stage records and deposits do not add into customer counts
task: Reconcile cash, revenue and deposits, then state commercial readiness.

facts.S-CRM: One cohort has twelve inquiries, eight quotes, four bookings and three signed orders; these stages overlap. Two signed customers paid USD 250 deposits. Customer A later paid the USD 750 balance and accepted the USD 1000 service. Customer B's service has not begun.
facts.S-OPERATIONS: Receipts are verified. A's actual costs and obligations are reconciled; support, permissions, next-cycle capacity and an accountable owner are documented. Only A has received delivery. No additional collections or earned revenue exist.

anchors: Treats funnel stages as overlapping evidence and identifies two paying customers but only one accepted completed cycle.
Separates gross collections, earned revenue and the outstanding undelivered customer deposit correctly.
Supports a scoped MVC claim for A's offer while preserving B's obligation and avoiding repeatability or broad-demand claims.
alternatives: A conservative paid-cycle description is valid if it preserves the supplied operating evidence.

title: Scheduled remittance is not verified collection
task: Revise the launch status statement and identify the evidence needed for the remaining commitment.

facts.S-DELIVERY: A customer signed a USD 6000 contract and accepted the delivered work. The invoice was issued yesterday. Support, actual delivery costs, capacity and the next owner are documented.
facts.S-PAYMENT: The customer sent an image showing a transfer scheduled for tomorrow. Today's reconciled bank and processor records show no receipt. The draft status says 'paid MVC demonstrated and cash available for hiring.' The operator is commissioned to review status, not move money or contact anyone.

anchors: Recognizes the accepted delivery and contract while identifying collection as unverified and not yet available cash.
Removes the paid MVC and available-cash claims pending actual receipt reconciliation.
Specifies checking the resulting payment record before the dependent hiring/cash commitment, within review-only authority.
alternatives: Describing the work as delivered and accepted with payment pending is sufficient; there is no need to redo unrelated gates.

title: A cost-center transfer accompanies a valid department cycle
task: Write the correct operating status and assess the proposed revenue claim.

facts.S-INTERNAL: An internal routing service completed a cycle accepted by the receiving operations lead and accountable sponsor. Actual staff hours, authorized allocation, spending and outstanding obligations were reconciled. The next cycle has an owner, available staff, permission and a documented failure route.
facts.S-FINANCE: Finance posted USD 1200 between two cost centers under an approved USD 8000 departmental allocation. No external customer bought anything. The proposed board line is 'new business generated USD 1200 revenue and demonstrated a paid MVC.'

anchors: Recognizes the demonstrated department operating cycle from its acceptance, resources and continuation evidence.
Rejects treating the internal cost-center transfer as an external sale, cash receipt or paid commercial MVC.
Provides a usable scoped department status rather than blocking valid internal operation for missing commercial payment.
alternatives: The finance transfer may be reported as internal allocation or cost attribution if its basis is retained.

title: A refunded rejected delivery leaves a different claim
task: Assess the founder's completion claim and recommend the next safe experiment or recovery step.

facts.S-RECEIPTS: A customer paid USD 1200 for a report. The delivered file omitted a required region, and the customer explicitly rejected it. The founder agreed to cancel; the full refund is verified. No revised scope or second delivery was accepted.
facts.S-STATUS: The founder proposes 'first paid cycle completed; repeat immediately.' The operator may analyze the failure and draft a corrected scope. Further customer work requires a new agreement. The original acceptance criterion included every region.

anchors: Retains the original payment as evidence of initial willingness while reporting rejection, cancellation and the completed refund.
Rejects a completed accepted MVC cycle or net retained collection claim for this engagement.
Preserves the failed acceptance criterion and recommends a corrected bounded offer or recovery design before renewed delivery.
alternatives: Walking away from this offer is valid if tied to the delivery defect and remaining capability rather than erasing the evidence.

title: A paid bespoke success lacks an available next operator
task: Determine what has been demonstrated and whether the next identical sale is operationally supportable.

facts.S-CYCLE: An unrelated customer paid USD 8000 and accepted a bespoke analysis. Verified tool costs were USD 500. The founder supplied eighty unpaid hours, including repeated manual repairs. Those hours were logged but omitted from the draft capacity assessment.
facts.S-CONTINUATION: Only the founder knows the repair process and will be unavailable for two months. No handoff procedure or trained substitute exists. The draft says 'repeatable MVC ready for immediate sales.' The task authorizes planning only.

anchors: Acknowledges the accepted paid customer delivery without converting one bespoke success into repeatability.
Includes the founder's unpaid work as real capacity and identifies the unavailable operator and missing handoff as continuation blockers.
Recommends a concrete capability transfer, bounded redesign or later commitment before promising immediate repetition.
alternatives: A scoped paid-cycle statement is valid while withholding full operating-readiness claims until continuation is feasible.

title: Profitable accepted work can still fail a cash floor
task: Reconcile contribution and cash; assess an immediate USD 450 contractor payment against the owner's rule.

facts.S-LEDGER: The current period opens with USD 1000 unrestricted cash. An accepted project earns USD 2000: a USD 500 deposit was collected, and USD 1500 is due next month. Variable delivery costs incurred are USD 600, of which USD 200 is paid now and USD 400 is due next month. Fixed cash costs now are USD 300. No other flows exist.
facts.S-RULE: The owner permits the additional contractor payment only if current closing cash stays at or above USD 800.

anchors: Separates earned revenue and incurred variable costs from their receipt and payment timing.
Computes cash and contribution while retaining the next-month receivable and payable.
Holds or defers the USD 450 payment because it breaches the floor, without treating contribution as spendable cash.
alternatives: A smaller payment may be proposed, subject to revised contractor terms.

title: A free trial demonstrates use within its observed scope
task: Draft an evidence-bound update and choose the next experiment for the founder's pricing decision.

facts.S-TRIAL: Six target users joined a deliberately free reconciliation trial. Three completed the workflow and accepted their outputs. Logged before-and-after task times support a two-hour saving for each of those three users. The others never supplied data.
facts.S-COMMERCIAL: No price was shown, no purchasing owner was asked, and no money changed hands. The founder must decide whether to offer a paid version. Preparation of one explicit offer is authorized; outreach is not.

anchors: Reports observed use, accepted delivery and measured savings only for the three completing users.
Does not turn free participation, acceptance or savings into price acceptance or verified paid demand.
Proposes a bounded priced offer to relevant purchasing owners with prospective criteria for the pricing decision.
alternatives: Investigating noncompletion first is valid if the recommendation explains why that adoption risk should precede a paid test.

title: Repeat delivery to one buyer supports a narrow repetition claim
task: Write a readiness statement for the next engagement and evaluate the founder's expansion language.

facts.S-CYCLES: The same customer purchased, paid for and accepted three monthly reports under the same scope and price. Each took the expected six operator hours, including support. Actual cash, costs and obligations are reconciled. A trained owner, spare capacity and permissions support the next cycle.
facts.S-DRAFT: The founder calls this 'repeatable delivery and scalable market demand across the sector.' No other buying unit has received an offer. Only a small next experiment is being planned.

anchors: Accepts evidence of repeated delivery and exchange for this customer, offer and observed conditions.
Limits independent demand evidence to one buying unit and rejects sector-wide scalable-demand inference.
Supports a bounded next engagement or new-buyer test using the available owner and capacity.
alternatives: Continuing the existing customer alone is valid when framed as operational continuation rather than market expansion proof.

title: Client purchasing funds are distinct from service payment
task: Correct the commercial evidence and available-cash statement for the printing procurement service.

facts.S-CONTRACT: The client transferred USD 10000 solely for the operator to purchase printing on the client's behalf. The contract requires unused funds returned and prohibits using them for the operator's expenses. A separate USD 600 service fee was also received and verified.
facts.S-DELIVERY: Printing has not been ordered or delivered, and the client has accepted no outcome. The founder reports 'USD 10600 service revenue collected; use the balance for payroll; MVC complete.' The commission is review only.

anchors: Separates restricted client purchasing funds from the verified service-fee payment and the operator's available working cash.
Does not classify the whole transfer as service revenue or authorize client funds for payroll.
Recognizes service-fee payment evidence while withholding completed-cycle claims until delivery, acceptance and operating requirements are met.
alternatives: The report may leave fee revenue recognition unresolved while clearly identifying verified fee collection and incomplete delivery.

title: Technical completion does not settle a commercial launch claim
task: Revise the launch memo's evidence statement and recommend the cheapest next test of the unresolved commercial assumption.

facts.S-BUILD: A prototype completed an internal demonstration, and all forty-two package checks passed. The founder produced a polished company pack. These checks concern installation and report formatting, not customer outcomes.
facts.S-MARKET: Three target operations managers described recent reconciliation problems and their existing manual work. No customer has used the prototype, received an offer or agreed to buy. The memo says 'operating company demonstrated with validated paying demand.' Drafting a bounded test is authorized.

anchors: Preserves the technical and reported-problem evidence while rejecting unsupported operating-company and paying-demand claims.
Identifies the missing intended-customer behavior and purchasing evidence rather than requiring more packaging work.
Proposes a bounded explicit offer or delivery experiment with an owner, observable criteria and an exposure cap.
alternatives: A manual service test is valid if it directly tests the intended outcome and purchasing decision without needing further prototype development.

title: Convert at the buying-unit level
task: Report outreach-to-purchase and outreach-to-response rates for the buying-unit hypothesis and interpret their limits.

facts.S-COHORT: The campaign contacted twenty-four distinct people at eight unrelated firms. Each firm has one purchasing budget and one decision process. Twelve people replied, representing five firms. Three of the eight firms independently bought and paid; multiple contacts within each purchased firm participated in discussions.
facts.S-HYPOTHESIS: The experiment asks whether a targeted firm will buy the standard offer. All eight firms received the same offer during the observation window. The account mapping and receipts are verified.

anchors: Uses eight unique buying units as the outreach denominator for this firm-level hypothesis.
Uses three purchased firms and five responding firms as numerators without inflating evidence from multiple contacts.
Interprets the results as this selected cohort's observed rates rather than a sector-wide demand estimate.
alternatives: Contact-level response can additionally be reported if separately labeled and not substituted for buying-unit conversion.

title: Ten locations share a single purchase decision
task: Assess the claim of ten independent buyers and recommend the evidence needed for the next market-expansion decision.

facts.S-STRUCTURE: Ten branch managers requested the service. A central procurement office controls the sole budget, selected the vendor once and signed one contract covering all branches. Branches cannot independently buy or reject that vendor.
facts.S-USE: All ten branches used the delivered service, and central procurement paid and accepted the contract. The founder proposes hiring a sales team because 'ten independent buyers converted.' No offer has reached a separately controlled purchasing unit.

anchors: Counts one independent purchasing decision while preserving ten locations as adoption or delivery evidence.
Rejects multiplying one central contract into ten independent buyer conversions or broad market validation.
Recommends a bounded test with another independently controlled buyer before using this evidence to justify broad sales expansion.
alternatives: Further branch rollout may be supported operationally if separately assessed; it does not create independent purchasing evidence.

title: Friendly volunteers do not represent the target segment
task: Choose the next research or offer test before the founder commits to an enterprise-only launch.

facts.S-SAMPLE: Eight webinar volunteers discussed the concept. Six are friends of the organizer and work at small firms outside the proposed enterprise segment. Two are enterprise practitioners with no purchasing authority. Five volunteers praised the idea; no recent purchasing decision or spend was documented.
facts.S-CHOICE: The founder proposes an enterprise-only launch based on the five positive reactions. The operator can prepare one week of research or a bounded offer test using permitted public role descriptions and synthetic examples.

anchors: Identifies recruitment, segment mismatch and purchasing-role limits behind the positive reactions.
Does not generalize five favorable comments to enterprise purchasing demand or impose a universal interview count.
Proposes a targeted next test reaching relevant enterprise users and buying authority with recent behavior or an explicit offer.
alternatives: Reconsidering the enterprise segment is valid if framed as a hypothesis requiring evidence, not a conclusion that smaller firms will pay.

title: Payment month is not the offer cohort
task: Calculate cohort purchase rates as of June 30 and advise how to compare the two offer cohorts.

facts.S-COHORTS: Ten unique buying units received priced offers in May. Eight different units received priced offers in June. During June, five units paid: three from the May cohort and two from the June cohort. No other payments occurred.
facts.S-STATUS: May has four pending and three declined offers; June has five pending and one declined. May offers had thirty more days of observation. The founder divides all five June payments by the eight June offers and calls that the June cohort rate.

anchors: Assigns payments to the buying units' offer cohorts rather than mixing payment-period numerators with offer-period denominators.
Reports the correct as-of rates and preserves outstanding outcomes in each cohort.
Qualifies performance comparison for different observation maturity rather than declaring a price or market effect.
alternatives: Reporting five June collections separately as payment-period activity is valid alongside cohort conversion.

title: A common parent can contain separately controlled buying units
task: Define the relevant unit of evidence and assess how much independent purchasing support the three contracts provide.

facts.S-AUTHORITY: Two subsidiaries of one parent each have separate budgets and accountable purchasing owners. Each independently evaluated the offer, could decline without affecting the other and signed its own contract. There was no parent mandate or shared procurement decision. An unrelated firm also independently purchased.
facts.S-SCOPE: The hypothesis concerns independently controlled budget owners buying the same service. All three contracts have verified payment. The report currently collapses the subsidiaries automatically because they share a parent.

anchors: Recognizes three separately controlled purchase decisions for the stated budget-owner hypothesis using the supplied authority evidence.
Discloses the shared parent and potential correlation rather than claiming three unrelated corporate groups.
Keeps legal-organization counts distinct from buying-unit counts and avoids automatic merging solely by parent identity.
alternatives: Reporting two corporate groups alongside three autonomous buying units is valid if the units and inference limits are explicit.

title: Survey percentages retain their response-conditioned denominators
task: Prepare an honest survey summary and recommend the next follow-up for the paid-offer decision.

facts.S-SURVEY: Forty qualified, unrelated buying units were approached. Twenty replied. Twelve respondents said they have some relevant budget, and four respondents asked whether paid pilots are available. No respondent received a price, accepted an offer or paid.
facts.S-DRAFT: The team describes the result as 'sixty percent of our market is ready to pay.' It wants response rate, respondent budget-claim rate and paid-pilot inquiry rate among all approached units. Preparing a reply is authorized.

anchors: Uses the specified denominator for each rate and identifies budget statements as self-reports among respondents.
Rejects market-wide extrapolation and treats paid-pilot questions as inquiries rather than payment or accepted prices.
Proposes an explicit bounded offer to relevant inquirers or budget owners to test the next commercial step.
alternatives: An additional respondent inquiry rate is valid if labeled separately from the requested all-approached rate.

title: Silence is not a retrospective eligibility exclusion
task: Decide whether the original test passed and specify how to record its outcome and any next experiment.

facts.S-PREDECLARED: The test includes twenty firms with ten to fifty seats and succeeds if at least three pay within two weeks. All twenty met that eligibility rule and received the same offer. Two paid, six declined and twelve were silent by the deadline.
facts.S-REVISION: After seeing results, the founder proposes excluding the twelve silent firms as 'unqualified because not engaged,' reporting only the eight responders, and marking the original test successful. A revised follow-up experiment may be drafted.

anchors: Retains all twenty eligible exposed firms in the original cohort despite nonresponse.
Records failure against the original three-payment criterion without retrospective threshold or eligibility changes.
Permits a separately labeled responder analysis or amended follow-up while preserving the original result and decision basis.
alternatives: A new engagement-focused test is valid if its criteria are set prospectively and it does not replace the historical outcome.

title: Web activity and qualified buyers measure different funnels
task: Calculate quote-to-purchase and qualified-lead-to-purchase rates, then assess the proposed website conversion claim.

facts.S-ANALYTICS: The page logged 1200 sessions: 200 confirmed bots and 1000 human sessions from 700 unique browser users. Browser identities cannot be mapped reliably to firms or purchasing roles.
facts.S-CRM: Forty verified unique buying units requested details. Ten of those units received a priced quote; four of those ten purchased and paid. All belong to one closed observation cohort. The founder calls four purchases divided by 700 browser users the target-firm conversion rate.

anchors: Uses ten quoted buying units and forty qualified buying units for the two requested stage rates.
Keeps sessions, browser users and buying units distinct rather than treating them as interchangeable denominators.
Rejects the target-firm website conversion inference because browser-to-firm eligibility and identity are unknown.
alternatives: A descriptive purchase-per-browser-user metric may be disclosed with strong unit limitations, without relabeling it firm conversion.

title: Zero delivered offers cannot estimate offer rejection
task: Interpret the experiment outcome and recommend the next permitted step before changing the offer.

facts.S-RECEIPT: Twelve qualified prospects were queued to receive a priced offer. The mail service rejected every send before delivery. Delivery receipts confirm zero offers reached recipients. There were no replies or purchases.
facts.S-REPORT: The spreadsheet records zero percent conversion and concludes that the price was rejected by all twelve prospects. The owner permits diagnosing the sending failure and preparing a corrected test; retrying outbound messages is not part of this commission.

anchors: Distinguishes a failed exposure mechanism from an observed response to the priced offer.
Treats purchase conversion among delivered offers as undefined or unestimable with a zero delivered denominator.
Recommends verifying delivery in a corrected authorized test without claiming price rejection or performing an uncommissioned retry.
alternatives: Zero purchases among the queued list can be reported descriptively if the complete delivery failure and inference limit are explicit.

title: Two independent cycles can justify one bounded next customer
task: Decide whether the founder's next-customer plan meets the predeclared rule and state the evidence limits.

facts.S-RULE: Before testing, the owner set a rule: one paid, accepted cycle with reconciled obligations and feasible continuation permits preparing one additional customer slot within the existing cap. Broader hiring or market-wide claims are outside the decision.
facts.S-RESULT: Two unrelated buying units independently bought, paid and accepted the same offer. Costs, support, permissions and next-cycle ownership are reconciled. Capacity supports exactly one additional slot. Only these two buyers were interviewed, and no wider market sample exists.

anchors: Recognizes that the supplied results satisfy the specific predeclared rule for preparing one additional slot.
Does not impose an arbitrary interview minimum or deny the verified independent purchase and acceptance evidence.
Limits the recommendation to existing authority and capacity without claiming market-wide demand, scalable growth or permission to hire.
alternatives: A cautious Proceed for preparation is valid alongside explicit small-sample limits; an unbounded expansion recommendation is not.
